transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Wu (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO - Nova Labs), Marco Ruiz (ML Eng), Liz Chen (Infra)

Summary: Quick discovery on Redwood PLG quickstart, clarifying hosted vs dedicated vs private options, time-to-first-token, free credits, and initial perf benchmarks. Customer is evaluating for embedding/search and chat features inside their product; primary concerns are latency, cost, and data residency.

00:00 Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, with Daniel our solutions engineer.
00:06 Aisha: Hey thanks, yeah excited to learn more — we're looking to move from an in-house inference setup to something less ops heavy.
00:10 Daniel: Great, quick agenda — get a sense of current stack, use cases, perf goals, then show how the PLG quickstart works and what Dedicated/Private would look like.
00:18 Marco: Quick note — we care about P95 latency under 120ms for small chat completions, and embeddings at scale, like 200 qps.
00:25 Liz: And on infra side we have strict VPC requirements, SSO via SAML, and need audit logs for compliance.
00:30 Samira: Totally — that maps to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs. For PLG/self-serve the hosted API gets you running fastest — sign up, get API key, do a curl, first token in seconds. We also give trial credits by default for teams.
00:42 Aisha: How much are the trial credits?
00:44 Samira: We typically provision $500 in credits for evaluation but can adjust per account.
00:48 Marco: When you say "first token in seconds" — is that realistic for our corp environment? Any onboarding hoops like IP allowlists, VPC peering?
00:55 Daniel: For the hosted quickstart no VPC peering is required — it's public API. You sign up, confirm email, create API key in console, you can run the example curl or SDK snippet — we've seen devs hit first token within 30–90 seconds depending on network. If you need VPC or private control plane, that's where Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) comes in and that takes more setup.
01:15 Aisha: Ok. For data residency we might need EU-only — is that supported on hosted?
01:20 Samira: Hosted supports region-specific endpoints — EU region available. For strict residency or air-gapped, Private is the route. Dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud with isolation and can be region pinned.
01:30 Liz: Re SSO and audit logs — are those in hosted?
01:32 Daniel: Hosted has SSO and audit logs for org-level accounts, but for advanced compliance (custom KMS/HSM, deeper network controls) customers move to Private.
01:40 Marco: Can you do canary rollouts with model versions? We run A/B tests across models and quantization profiles.
01:44 Daniel: Yes — rollouts, model pinning, and fallback policies are first-class in the platform. You can route by latency/cost/region and fallback to a cheaper variant if capacity's constrained.
01:52 Aisha: Cost — how do we reason about latency vs cost? If we want P95 under 120ms that sounds expensive.
01:57 Samira: It's a spectrum — Dedicated reserved capacity gives better predictable unit costs. Hosted you pay per-token; we provide batching, prefix caching, and quantized variants to reduce per-token cost. Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization profiles based on your workload.
02:10 Marco: You mentioned KV cache — can you explain?
02:12 Daniel: Sure. KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in older notes) is the key-value cache for transformer k-v pairs. We persist prefix KV across sessions when appropriate to avoid recomputation which reduces tokens and latency.
02:24 Aisha: Is the KV cache compatible across model versions?
02:27 Daniel: Usually yes within the same model family and compatible kernels; when crossing architectures you'd warm the cache.
02:32 Liz: Are there any max sequence length or memory constraints we should know for embeddings or chat?
02:36 Daniel: We expose the model's sequence length; larger contexts increase GPU memory. For embeddings the vectors are constant size but throughput depends on batch. We'll recommend kernels and quantization for your typical payload shapes during the benchmark.
02:48 Marco: Onbenchmarks — can we run a head-to-head with our sample payloads? We want to see p95 and cost/unit.
02:53 Daniel: Absolutely — typical flow: you give sample payloads + QPS target, we run benchmarks on hosted and dedicated configs, share latency/cost profiles and recommendations. We'll need a small dataset from you and authorization to run the tests under a temporary trial key.
03:05 Aisha: About security — SOC2? ISO? Key management?
03:08 Samira: Redwood is SOC2 compliant and we offer ISO attestation for enterprise. For KMS we integrate with cloud KMS providers and can do customer-managed keys in Private.
03:18 Liz: Do you store customer data? Retention policies?
03:20 Daniel: By default, hosted may retain minimal logs for troubleshooting; we have options for no retention and strict controls for Dedicated/Private. We'll share our security whitepaper.
03:28 Aisha: Ok. What's the difference in time-to-production between Hosted and Dedicated?
03:31 Samira: Hosted: minutes to hours for basic quickstart; Dedicated: a few days to provision reserved capacity and autoscaling policies; Private: weeks depending on on-prem or VPC integration.
03:42 Marco: For Dedicated, do we reserve GPUs and get stable latency guarantees?
03:45 Daniel: Yes — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, SLA-backed targets, and autoscaling config. Good for steady high-volume workloads.
03:54 Aisha: For PLG we want to self-serve initially and maybe move to Dedicated. How does the quickstart support that path?
03:59 Samira: The experience is unified — same API surface and model catalog across modes. You can start on hosted with free credits, validate integration and user flows, then migrate traffic to Dedicated while keeping the same API keys/route configs (we help coordinate).
04:12 Marco: Any gotchas with SDKs and streaming responses? We use streaming in our chat UI.
04:16 Daniel: We support streaming responses and SDKs for JS/Python. On streaming there are network considerations for low-latency websockets vs SSE — we can share best-practices.
04:26 Aisha: About pricing, can you send a sample for a small PLG/seed stage usage? We want a ballpark for hosted token pricing and Dedicated sizing.
04:31 Samira: I'll send a pricing sheet after the call with hosted per-token estimates and an example Dedicated commitment for 2–4 GPUs. We'll include an ROI example and when Dedicated becomes cost-effective.
04:40 Liz: Does the quickstart include sample app templates? We prefer a reference widget for chat + embeddings search.
04:44 Samira: Yes, quickstart repo includes examples: token-based curl, JS chat widget, and an embeddings vector search starter. We'll link to the GitHub and the console quickstart flow.
04:52 Marco: Any limits on trial keys? QPS caps?
04:55 Daniel: Trial keys have soft rate limits to prevent abuse; we can raise them for benchmark sessions.
05:00 Aisha: Ok this is helpful. A few clarification questions: for EU-only hosted, is billing in USD or EUR and can we have invoice terms?
05:07 Samira: We support invoicing and enterprise billing; region billing currency can be discussed with the account team.
05:12 Marco: For model variants, do you host open models or proprietary ones?
05:15 Daniel: We host curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles; some partners may also be available. We do not surface 3rd-party closed models unless under license.
05:25 Aisha: Are there any prerequisites on our side to get trial access?
05:27 Samira: Just sign-up and a quick verification. For Dedicated/Private we'd need procurement and some network info.
05:32 Samira: Ok quick recap and next steps — Samira to send pricing + quickstart guide + security doc, Daniel to share benchmark checklist and request sample payloads, Nova to provide sample dataset and targets. We'll provision a $500 trial credit and trial API key.
05:45 Aisha: Sounds good, let's aim to get the benchmark scheduled next Wednesday.
05:48 Samira: I'll send calendar invite once we confirm availability. Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: some terms may be slightly off (K-V cash vs KV cache) and occasional dropped punctuation.

References & links mentioned: Redwood quickstart repo (link shared in chat), security whitepaper (link to be sent), pricing workbook (link to be sent).

End of transcript.
